extracted.intended_audience: researchers (Principal Investigators) and Host Institutions preparing ERC Synergy Grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for applying to ERC Synergy Grants: multi-PI proposals (2–4 PIs) addressing ambitious research problems, including eligibility, host institution requirements, ethics, evaluation steps, and funding rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can apply — number and role of PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: A group of two to maximum four Principal Investigators (PIs) working together and bringing different skills and resources to tackle ambitious research problems. One will be designated as the corresponding PI (cPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synergy Grants support projects carried out by a group of two to four individual researchers. Ensure each PI's role and complementary expertise are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility regarding academic training
rubrics_metrics.description: No specific eligibility criteria regarding the academic training are foreseen for ERC Synergy Grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus eligibility on the scientific case and track record rather than formal degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI track record requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PIs must present a competitive track record as appropriate to their career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide CVs and track records that demonstrate the PIs' ability to deliver the proposed ambitious research; evidence should be appropriate to each PI's career stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole evaluation criterion — scientific excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated on the sole criterion of scientific excellence which takes on the additional meaning of outstanding intrinsic synergetic effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the research project and the Principal Investigators are assessed on excellence; explicitly demonstrate the synergetic effect produced by the team beyond individual contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate that project cannot be done by a single PI
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must demonstrate that the proposed research cannot be carried out by a single PI working alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the combination of PIs, skills, resources, and collaborative approach is necessary to achieve the objectives; make the added value of Synergy explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research location and Host Institution (HI) jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must be conducted by all PIs in a public or private research organisation (Host Institution, HI) established in one of the EU Member States or associated countries. One PI per group can be hosted or engaged by an institution outside the EU or associated countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the geographic and legal status of each HI; if one PI is outside EU/associated countries, ensure the rest of the team meet location requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution support letters at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: At submission stage, all Host Institutions must provide the host support letter for their Principal Investigator(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and include signed host support letters from each HI with the submission; absence may affect eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution commitments and awardee HI
rubrics_metrics.description: The ERC Synergy Grant is awarded to the cHI that engages and hosts the cPI for at least the duration of the grant, and to any other HI that engages and hosts other PIs participating in the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the cHI and other HIs commit to host the PIs for the full grant duration; clarify which institution will be the cHI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host Institution obligations during the grant
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institutions must engage the PIs for at least the duration of the grant and must offer appropriate conditions for PIs supported to independently direct the proposed research and manage the project's funding for its duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional commitments to PI independence, research conditions, and financial management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary agreement requirement if PI not yet at HI
rubrics_metrics.description: The PIs do not necessarily need to be working at the HI indicated in the proposal at submission. However, a mutual agreement — called supplementary agreement — and the host institutions' commitment on how the relationship will be established are necessary, should the proposal be successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a PI will move to the HI after award, provide a supplementary agreement describing terms and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and staff nationality/location
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC Synergy grants support projects by groups of PIs who can employ researchers of any nationality as team members; it is possible to have team members located in a third country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may include international staff and remote team members; justify their roles and how coordination will work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum funding and project duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Synergy Grants can be up to a maximum of €10 million for a period of 6 years (pro rata for projects of shorter duration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set project duration and requested budget within these limits; if shorter than 6 years, budget should be pro rata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional funding for major costs
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional €4 million can be requested in the proposal in total to cover eligible 'start-up' costs for researchers moving from a third country to the EU or an associated country and/or the purchase of major equipment and/or access to large facilities and/or other major experimental and field work costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicable, justify and itemise start-up, major equipment, large-facility access, or major fieldwork costs when requesting the additional €4M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost coverage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An ERC grant can cover up to 100% of the total eligible direct costs of the research plus a contribution of 25% of the total eligible costs towards indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare budget lines under eligible direct costs and calculate the 25% flat-rate contribution for indirect costs accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call-based submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grant applications can only be submitted in response to a Call for Proposals. The ERC has annual calls for proposals covering all scientific fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only to open calls; check the specific Synergy call documents for that year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete application contents
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ERC grant application to be complete, it needs to include the administrative forms, the research proposal and the supplementary documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assemble all required parts (administrative forms, Parts A/B of proposal, annexes, host support letters, etc.) before submission; incomplete proposals risk rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission system and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must be submitted through the EU submission service by the specified closing date. You can update your submitted proposal any time before the deadline by submitting a new version which overwrites the old one. Deadlines cannot be changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarise yourself with the EU submission service and submit well before the deadline; you will receive an acknowledgement of receipt by e-mail for each submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission planning tasks
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the call is published: find which ERC grant and which call is suitable, think who could be a suitable PI to complement your expertise, each PI should identify their Host Institutions (portability applies to each PI), identify further team members and justify their presence, and obtain the written consent of any researcher mentioned in the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work early with proposed PIs and HIs, justify team composition in the proposal, and gather written consents and institutional agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation process structure — three steps and interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: A single submission of the full proposal is followed by a three-step evaluation, including interviews. Synergy evaluations will be unique, fit for complex projects and without predefined panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for multi-step assessment: initial filtering, in-depth review, and interview; structure proposal to perform at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation applies excellence to PIs and synergetic aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated by selected international peer reviewers who evaluate proposals on the basis of excellence as the sole criterion. It applies to the evaluation of both the research project and the Principal Investigators, taking into account the synergetic aspects of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address both the project's intrinsic scientific excellence and how the PIs together create synergies that elevate the project beyond individual efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 evaluation scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Part I of the scientific proposal and the Principal Investigators’ Curriculum Vitae (CV) and Track Record will be assessed by the evaluation panel (and not the full scientific proposal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure Part I and CV/track records concisely present the case to pass initial filtering; make synergetic rationale and PI credentials prominent in Part I.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 evaluation scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete version of the Research proposal will be assessed (CVs and Track record, Parts I and II of the Scientific Proposal, Resources and Time commitment and Budget table annex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full methodological detail, resource justification, time commitment statements for each PI, and a clear budget annex to support claims in Parts I and II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 3 evaluation — interview and final selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators will be invited for an interview to present their project to a panel in Brussels and the most competitive of the retained proposals will be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a concise, well-rehearsed presentation and plan for the interview; panels may be reconfigured to ensure appropriate expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition and selection of evaluation panels
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel Members are selected by the ERC Scientific Council on the basis of their scientific reputation. The step 1 panel is formed from approximately 90 panel members and chairs. Five to seven panels in step 2 will be formed dynamically after the step 1 filtering to ensure the best expertise for the retained proposals. External remote experts provide specialised input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect multidisciplinary panels and external remote evaluators; tailor language to be clear to generalists while including specialised detail for remote experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality threshold, scoring and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who pass the quality threshold at step 3 - scored 'A' - are ranked. Depending on the call budget available, a budgetary cut-off applies to the ranking list and only the highest ranked proposals are offered an ERC grant until the call's budget has been exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for top ranking by maximizing excellence arguments; even scoring 'A' does not guarantee funding if beyond budgetary cut-off.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact policy for reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are requested not to contact reviewers under any circumstances as they risk having their proposal rejected from the evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to identify or contact panel members or reviewers; use official communication channels only (NCP or ERC applicants' mailbox).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review requirement and legal basis
rubrics_metrics.description: If your proposal is selected for funding it will undergo an ethics review. This is a legal requirement under the Horizon Europe Framework Programme - Regulation 2021/695: Eligible actions and ethical principles (Article 18) and Ethics (Article 19). The basis for this ethics review is Part A (including the Ethics Issues Table – EIT – and the Ethics Self-Assessment – ESA) and Part B of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete Part A (EIT and ESA) thoroughly at submission to streamline ethics review; reference relevant laws and ethical principles as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics Self-Assessment (ESA) importance
rubrics_metrics.description: A well-detailed ESA is crucial to facilitate the process as it clarifies what issues are linked to the proposed research activities and how these will be dealt with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear descriptions of potential ethics issues and concrete mitigation/management plans in the ESA to reduce follow-up during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics review stages and applicant responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The ethics review comprises 3 stages: Ethics pre-screening (internal by ERCEA staff) to clear proposals without ethics issues or with simple ethics issues; Ethics screening (panels of independent ethics reviewers) to identify proposals with potentially Serious and/or Complex ethics issues — applicants might be contacted to provide additional information and are typically given 3 weeks to reply; Ethics assessment (panels of independent ethics reviewers) to discuss Serious and/or Complex ethics issues — ethics deliverables might be formulated for follow-up during project implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to respond to screening requests within the typical 3-week deadline and to produce ethics deliverables if required; for complex ethical issues plan for additional documentation and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific ethics requirement for hESCs
rubrics_metrics.description: Research proposals involving the use of hESCs will need to undergo all of the steps of the Ethics review and also a specific EC approval following a consultation to the HE programme committee comitology procedure, as this is a legal requirement under HE framework programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the proposal involves human embryonic stem cells, allow extra time and documentation for the specific EC approval process via comitology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feedback timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: External experts evaluate all the eligible proposals. About 4-5 months after the call deadline, you receive a letter from the ERC informing you on the result of the first step evaluation. At each of the three steps of the evaluation process you get feedback about the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect first-step feedback ~4–5 months after deadline and further feedback at each evaluation step; plan project timelines accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where calls and supporting documents are published
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls are published on this page, the EU Funding & Tenders Portal and in the Official Journal of the European Union. After the call opening, the names of the panel chairs and panel members are published on the ERC website. Key documents include the ERC Work Programme, Information to Applicants to the Synergy call, ERC Guide for Peer reviewers, Gender Equality Plans guidance and bias awareness material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult call-specific documents (Work Programme, Info to Applicants) and reviewer guides to align proposal structure and content with evaluation expectations; review published panel composition where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ERC data platforms for benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: You can use the ERC dashboard and the ERC Research Information System (ERIS) to search and analyze ERC funded projects and evaluated proposals, filter by criteria, export data, and examine project outputs & bibliometrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these platforms to benchmark prior funded Synergy projects, identify relevant expertise, and support claims about novelty or feasibility where appropriate.
